title: Change record
description: Everything one pull request's description, commit message and review replies say, held once. A field marked x-rewritable holds wording an editor may change; every other field is a fact.
$comment: Every pattern here closes with (?![\s\S]), which matches only where no character follows. A closing $ also matches before a final newline in some regex engines, so a value with a newline after it would pass there.

number.description: The pull request number. Null until the pull request is open.

title.description: The pull request title. Only its wording may be rewritten; its type, component and bracketed id are facts.

type.description: The commit type. It decides which sections the pull request body carries.

component.description: The thing a reader would search for, such as a package or skill name. Never a tracker id.

head_sha.description: The commit the verification gates ran at, as forty hex characters. Empty until known.

work_item.description: The tracker item this pull request delivers.

id.description: The tracker's full id for the item.

gloss.description: What the item is for, as the words that follow its id in a sentence.

slice.description: Which part of its parent item this pull request is, in one line.

summary.description: The opening of the pull request body: the problem, then what is true now, then what remains.

heads_up.description: Anything that should lower a reader's confidence, one sentence each. A list with nothing to say holds the single entry "None.". An entry that opens with a generator's name and a colon was written by that generator and is not rewritable.

where_this_fits.description: Where the work item sits in the tracker and among other pull requests. Generated from the tracker and from GitHub, never typed.

ancestry.description: The chain of parent items, outermost first, ending at the work item.

type.description: The tracker's type for the item, such as milestone or epic.

builds_on.description: Merged pull requests this one depends on.

concurrent.description: Open pull requests that touch a path this one touches.

scope.description: The parts of the parent item and the state of each.

slice.description: The part's tracker id or label.

pr.description: The open pull request delivering a part that is in flight.

digest.description: The generator's stamp over the rest of this group.

risk.description: What could go wrong, as a table.

reaches_outside_package.description: True when the change affects anything outside its own package. A true value calls for both blast-radius diagrams, or on a spec pull request for the items the spec mints.

failure.description: What could go wrong, as a user or agent would notice it.

evidence.description: How we know it did not happen: a named check and what it showed.

recovery.description: What to do if it did.

blast_radius.description: What the change reaches: two Mermaid diagram sources, written without their fences, or on a spec pull request the items the spec mints.

reach_graph.description: A graph from the changed component outward, each edge labelled by its kind of impact.

task_flow.description: The affected task flow with the changed steps marked.

mints.description: The tracker items a spec mints, which are a spec pull request's blast radius.

id.description: The item's tracker id. Left out until the item is minted.

what.description: What the item is, such as its title.

changes.description: What is different now, one entry per topic.

topic.description: A short label, written without its closing full stop.

design_notes.description: Why this approach, and each rejected alternative with what breaks under it.

discovered.description: Work found along the way and not done here.

rows.description: One entry per piece of work. A pull request that found nothing holds the single entry "None.".

item.description: The tracker id of a filed row.

pr.description: The pull request an in-flight row belongs to.

what.description: What the work is. On an in-flight row, what this pull request told the other one.

reason.description: Why it is not in this pull request. On a filed row the reason is the tracker's and is not rewritable.

filed_digest.description: The generator's stamp over the filed rows, which are generated from the tracker and never typed.

verification.description: The gates that ran and what did not.

not_run.description: Each check that was not run, and why. A list with nothing to say holds the single entry "None.".

campaign.description: Every review round on the pull request. Generated from the posted review verdicts, never typed.

rounds.description: The rounds the reviewer ran, as a range.

findings.description: The number of distinct findings. Comments and commits are not counted.

terminal_sha.description: The head of the latest complete round with no blocking finding. Empty when no round is.

claim_id.description: The completion claim the finding's round judged. Finding ids start again with each claim, so the claim is part of what names a finding.

artifact_class.description: The kind of artifact the finding's round reviewed. Finding ids start again with each kind, so the kind is part of what names a finding.

round.description: The round the finding first appeared in.

disposition.description: The latest disposition. Absent while the finding has none.

reason.description: The evidence given with that disposition.

work_item.description: The tracker item a deferred or transferred finding went to.

commit.description: The commit the author's reply names. Empty when the reply names none.

digest.description: The generator's stamp over the rest of this group.

criteria.description: The acceptance criteria as a table. A spec pull request holds one line instead, saying whether its criteria were attacked and where the attack record is.

promise.description: What the criterion promises, in plain words.

evidence.description: A test, a measurement or a review id.

commit.description: The commit message the merge uses.

subject.description: The whole first line. Only its wording may be rewritten; its type, component and bracketed id are facts.

why.description: The problem and who it affected.

verification.description: The decisive check and its observed result, and what was not run.

trivial.description: The reason the message has no body. Present only in place of why, change and verification.

attribution.description: Who wrote the change with the author.

co_author.description: The model and its vendor's no-reply address, as the co-author trailer's value.

session_key.description: The session trailer's key, which the authoring tool defines.

replies.description: One reply per review finding the author answers on the pull request.

claim_id.description: The completion claim the finding belongs to. A reply answers a campaign finding only when it gives the finding's claim, artifact class and id.

artifact_class.description: The kind of artifact the finding's round reviewed.

change.description: What is different now, in one or two sentences.

verification.description: The check and what it showed.

commit.description: The commit that made the change.

request_url.description: The reviewer comment that asked for a reply to a rejection.

record.description: The record's own bookkeeping. Written when the record is published or its wording is rewritten, never by the author.

revision.description: Zero until the record is first published.

digest.description: The digest of the record with this group removed.

comment_id.description: The pull request comment holding this revision.

head_sha.description: The pull request's head when the record was published.

rewrites.description: One entry per rewrite pass applied.
